slides.title: A Japanese officer kept fighting WWII until March 1974.
Orders: never surrender
slides.body: Hiroo Onoda, an army intelligence officer, reached Lubang Island in the Philippines in December 1944 with orders never to surrender.

slides.title: Fake news, he decided
slides.body: He dismissed leaflets announcing Japan's 1945 surrender, and later newspapers, as enemy tricks. He and three comrades fought on in the hills.

slides.title: Found by a young traveler
slides.body: One comrade surrendered in 1950; two were killed, in 1954 and 1972. In February 1974 a young Japanese traveler, Norio Suzuki, found Onoda.

slides.title: Ordered home by a bookseller
slides.body: He would yield only to a superior's order. On 9 March 1974 his former commander, by then a bookseller, read it to him. Marcos pardoned him.

slides.title: The part the legend skips
slides.body: His group allegedly killed up to about 30 islanders. And he wasn't the last holdout: Teruo Nakamura was found on Morotai in December 1974.

caption: He spent almost 29 years refusing to believe the war was over. Only one thing could stop him: a direct order. Could you have convinced him?
xPost: Hiroo Onoda reached a Philippine island in 1944 with orders never to surrender, and dismissed news of Japan's 1945 surrender as an enemy trick. He stood down in March 1974, when his old commander, by then a bookseller, came and read him the order.
